subject: ela
intro: Analyze the impact of an author's choices.

items.prompt:
Where and when a story happens is the:
A) setting
B) title
C) margin

The order in which events are told is the story's:
A) sequence/structure
B) font
C) length

An author's decisions about how to build a story are their:
A) choices
B) errors
C) page count

An author sets a story of grief in a single unchanging room. This choice:
A) mirrors and reinforces the character's inescapable grief
B) has no effect
C) removes all emotion
items.answer: A) mirrors and reinforces the character's inescapable grief

steps: Setting mirrors theme. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) mirrors and reinforces the character's inescapable grief

items.prompt:
An author withholds a character's name until the final chapter. This choice:
A) keeps the character distant until the end, giving the final naming weight
B) immediately reveals everything
C) has no effect
items.answer: A) keeps the character distant until the end, giving the final naming weight

steps: Shapes reader's experience. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) keeps the character distant until the end, giving the final naming weight

items.prompt:
Why do an author's CHOICES about story elements matter?
A) each shapes the work's meaning and the reader's experience
B) they are random
C) only the length matters
items.answer: A) each shapes the work's meaning and the reader's experience

steps: Choices shape meaning. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) each shapes the work's meaning and the reader's experience

items.prompt:
An author tells a story through letters that only ever show one side of the correspondence. This choice MOST likely:
A) limits the reader to one perspective, creating gaps the reader must fill
B) reveals everyone's thoughts
C) has no effect on meaning
items.answer: A) limits the reader to one perspective, creating gaps the reader must fill

steps: Form shapes perspective. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) limits the reader to one perspective, creating gaps the reader must fill

items.prompt:
An author opens a tragedy with a cheerful, sunlit wedding. The MOST likely effect of this choice is to:
A) heighten the later tragedy by contrast
B) prove the story is a comedy
C) change the setting permanently
items.answer: A) heighten the later tragedy by contrast

solution.answer: A) heighten the later tragedy by contrast
